 JUDGMENT Wife, children, parents of deceased Kheta Ram and wife, children and father of deceased Kheema Ram filed applications under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 claiming compensation worth of Rs.1,50,00,000/- and Rs.50,00,000/- respectively, from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of car bearing No.KA-05- MU-9129 which are registered as MVC No.1035/2022 and MVC No.1036/2022 respectively, alleging that on SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 07.08.2021 at about 9.30 p.m., when Kheta Ram riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HV-9629 by keeping Kheema Ram on the pillion on 9th main road, Banashankai 2nd stage, Bengaluru, driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU- 9129 drove the same negligently from the opposite direction,
dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Kheta Ram and Kheema Ram/riders of the motorcycle.
2. Immediately after the accident, injured have been shifted to Seva Kshethra Hospital, wherein both succumbed to the injuries.
3. As on the date of accident, Kheta Ram being aged about 38 years, used to earn Rs.4,65,240/- p.a.,
by working as a carpenter and interior decorator and used to contribute entire income to the family.
As on the date of accident, Kheema Ram being aged about 28 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/- p.m.,
by working as a carpenter and used to contribute entire income to the family.
4.

Regarding the accident, Banashankari Traffic police registered a case in Crime No.61/2021 against the SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 driver of car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1/owner of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 appeared through her advocate and filed written statement denied the allegation regarding reason,
mode of accident, age, occupation and income of the deceased and submitted that the respondent No.2/insurance company is liable to pay compensation if any.

6. In respondent to the notice, the respondent No.2/insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 appeared through his advocate and filed written statement, denied the allegation regarding reason,
mode of accident, age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Respondent No.2 denied the liability Hiro vs Subha Venkatesh.J on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96526638/
3 to indemnify the respondent No.1 on the ground of violation of the terms of the policy.
7.

SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w  1036/2022  Issues in MVC No.1035/2022 1.Whether the Petitioners prove that due to rash and negligent driving of Hyundai Creta car bearing reg.No.KA05MU9129 by its driver dashed to the deceased Sri. Kheta Ram who was riding Bajaj Discover motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA05-HV-9629 and he succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 7/8/2021?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 and 2 proves that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of deceased himself ?
3.Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom ?
4.What order ?

sentences.text: In the light of the Judgments cited above with reference to the submissions made on behalf of both the parties, I have appreciated the material available in the file.

14. In the evidence PW.1 & 2 have stated that on 07.08.2021 at about 9.30 p.m., when Kheta Ram riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HV-9629 by keeping Kheema Ram on the pillion on 9th main road, Banashankai 2nd stage, Bengaluru, driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU- 9129 drove the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to the riders of the motorcycle.
PW.1 & 2 have stated that immediately SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 after the accident injured have been shifted to Seva Kshetra Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein both succumbed to the injuries.
15. In the written statement, the respondents No.1 & 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
In the cross-examination PW.1 Smt.Paramudevi w/o Kheta Ram and PW.2 Smt.Hiro w/o Kheema Ram submitted that they never witnessed the accident.

16. In the evidence, RW.1 Sr.Scientist, FSL, Madiwala, Bengaluru, stated about submission of report of the blood sample of Suhas S/o Venkatesh J.S.-driver of the car to the effect that the blood sample contained alcohol.

In the evidence affidavit, RW.2 an hearsay witness of the incident (Officer of insurance company) asserted that the person who drove the car during accident has committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 427, 304 of IPC and Sec.185 of the IMV Act (drove the car under intoxication).
In the cross-examination RW.2 submitted lack of personal knowledge about the incident pertaining to the case.

17. In the evidence affidavit RW.3/owner of the car stated that her son does not have the habit of consuming SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 alcohol and stated that in the claim petition as well as in the objection, insurance company falsely asserted that her son Suhas drove the car under intoxication.
IN the cross- examination RW.3 submitted that she never witnessed the accident.

18. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Cr.No.61/2021 registered by Banashankari Traffic police against Suhas S/o Venkatesh J.S., driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129, for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279, 304 of IPC and Sec.185 of MV Act, regarding the accident taken place between the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HV-9629 and car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 resulting in the death of Kheta Ram and Kheema Ram-riders of the motorcycle on the basis of the complaint presented by Omprakash S/o Parasuram.

Hence, I have concluded that on 07.08.2021 at about 9.30 p.m.,
when Kheta Ram riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA- 05-HV-9629 by keeping Kheema Ram on the pillion on 9th main road, Banashankai 2nd stage, Bengaluru, Suhas s/o Venkatesh J.S. S/o respondent No.1 negligently under intoxication drove the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 from the opposite direction, dashed the same to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HV-9629, then a BESCOM pole and a compound wall, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Kheta Ram and Kheema Ram/riders of the motorcycle who succumbed to those injuries.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in both the cases in SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 the Affirmative and Issue No.2 in both the cases in the Negative.
21. Issue No.3 in MVC No.1035/2022

In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that her husband had studied upto 8th standard.
PW.1 denied the suggestion about receipt of Rs.15 Lakhs as compensation towards personal accident claim from the insurance company of the motorcycle.
PW.1 stated that since last twenty years her husband worked as a carpenter.

26. Issue No.3 in MVC No.1036/2022 : In the evidence PW.2 Smt.Hiro w/o Kheema Ram stated that as on the date of accident her husband used to earn Rs.25,000/- p.m., by working as a carpenter and used to contribute entire income to the family.
27. In the written statement respondents No.1 & 2 denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of the deceased Kheema Ram.
In the cross-examination PW.2 SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 admitted non-production of documents regarding occupation, income of her husband.
In the evidence RW.1 to 3 stated nothing regarding occupation and income of Kheema Ram.
In the Aadhaar card, date of birth of Kheema Ram is noted as 01.07.1993 (28 years).
Birth Certificates, Aadhaar cards and other documents shows that the petitioners are the wife, children and father of Kheema Ram.

Hence, I have calculated loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased as on the date 28 years of accident - Notional Income of the deceased as on Rs.15,000/-
 the date of accident p.m.
 Add : 50% towards future prospects  of Kheema Ram (15,000 + 7,500  = 22,500/- )
 Less: 1/4th towards personal  expenses of Kheema Ram (22,500/-
 - 5,625/- = Rs.16,875/- )

Hence, I award Rs.34,42,500/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.2,20,000/-
(Rs.44,000/- x 5) towards loss of consortium.
Hence, the petitioners are entitle to receive a sum of Rs.36,95,500/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in MVC No.1036/2022 partly in the Affirmative.

29. Issue No.4 in both the cases : In the written statement, the respondent No.2/insurance company Hiro vs Subha Venkatesh.J on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96526638/
9 indirectly admitted his status as insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 asserting the status of the respondent No.1 as insured, however denied the liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 on the ground that the police have filed chargesheet against the driver of the car for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 427, 304 of IPC and Sec.185 of IMV Act ,i.e., driving of car under intoxication.

30. Chargesheet and enclosures shows that Suhas S/o respondent No.1 by keeping his cousin Krithika on the front left seat of the car drove the car under intoxication SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 and dashed the same to the motorcycle No.KA-05-HP- 9629, thereby caused accident, caused the death of Kheta Ram and Kheema Ram-riders of the motorcycle.
31. In these cases, there are no evidence to show that the respondent No.1 Shubha Venkatesh w/o Venkatesh J.S., mother of Suhas authorised her son to drive the car under intoxication.
The evidence available in the file are insufficient to infer the subsistence of mens-rea on the part of the respondent No.1 to authorise or permit Suhas to drive the car under intoxication.

32. Irrespective of the evidence available in the file, submissions made on behalf of both the parties,
on 17.09.2024, the respondent No.2/insurance company get filed application under Sec.170 of IMV Act, seeking permission to defend case on all the grounds available to the respondent No.1/insured/owner of the car.

When the respondent No.2/insurance company sought permission to defend the case on all the grounds available to respondent No.1/owner and insured of the car, it is also responsible to satisfy all the responsibilities of respondent No.1/owner/insured of the car.
Xerox copy of the DL SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 bearing No.KA0620130820625 dated 28.05.2013 shows that since 28.05.2013 Suhas had licence to drive light motor vehicle (Non-Transport).

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insured and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 are liable to pay compensation and awards are to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer Issue No.4 in both the cases accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The Petitions filed under Section 166 of IMV Act, by the petitioners are hereby partly allowed in the following terms:

In MVC No.1035/2022, the respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.75,99,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Lakhs Ninety Nine Thousand only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.

In MVC No.1036/2022, the respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.36,95,500/- (Rupees Thirty Six Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Five Hundred only) SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 shall deposit the compensation amount within three month from today.

Entire compensation amount and interest allocation in favour of petitioners No.2 to 4 (minors Kum.Varsha, Master Prathvi raj and Master Bhavesh)/children of deceased Kheta Ram, shall be deposited in any nationalised/scheduled bank in their names till they attain the age of 19 years,

dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Kheta Ram and Kheema Ram/riders of the motorcycle.
2. Immediately after the accident, injured have been shifted to Seva Kshethra Hospital, wherein both succumbed to the injuries.
3. As on the date of accident, Kheta Ram being aged about 38 years, used to earn Rs.4,65,240/- p.a.,
by working as a carpenter and interior decorator and used to contribute entire income to the family.
As on the date of accident, Kheema Ram being aged about 28 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/- p.m.,
by working as a carpenter and used to contribute entire income to the family.
4.

opennyai_summary.facts:
14. In the evidence PW.1 & 2 have stated that on 07.08.2021 at about 9.30 p.m., when Kheta Ram riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-HV-9629 by keeping Kheema Ram on the pillion on 9th main road, Banashankai 2nd stage, Bengaluru, driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU- 9129 drove the same negligently from the opposite direction, dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to the riders of the motorcycle.
In the cross-examination PW.1 Smt.Paramudevi w/o Kheta Ram and PW.2 Smt.Hiro w/o Kheema Ram submitted that they never witnessed the accident.
In the evidence affidavit, RW.2 an hearsay witness of the incident (Officer of insurance company) asserted that the person who drove the car during accident has committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 427, 304 of IPC and Sec.185 of the IMV Act (drove the car under intoxication).
In the cross-examination RW.2 submitted lack of personal knowledge about the incident pertaining to the case.
17. In the evidence affidavit RW.3/owner of the car stated that her son does not have the habit of consuming SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 alcohol and stated that in the claim petition as well as in the objection, insurance company falsely asserted that her son Suhas drove the car under intoxication.
IN the cross- examination RW.3 submitted that she never witnessed the accident.
Hence, the petitioners are entitle to receive a sum of Rs.36,95,500/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
30. Chargesheet and enclosures shows that Suhas S/o respondent No.1 by keeping his cousin Krithika on the front left seat of the car drove the car under intoxication SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 and dashed the same to the motorcycle No.KA-05-HP- 9629, thereby caused accident, caused the death of Kheta Ram and Kheema Ram-riders of the motorcycle.
31. In these cases, there are no evidence to show that the respondent No.1 Shubha Venkatesh w/o Venkatesh J.S., mother of Suhas authorised her son to drive the car under intoxication.
The evidence available in the file are insufficient to infer the subsistence of mens-rea on the part of the respondent No.1 to authorise or permit Suhas to drive the car under intoxication.
32. Irrespective of the evidence available in the file, submissions made on behalf of both the parties,
on 17.09.2024, the respondent No.2/insurance company get filed application under Sec.170 of IMV Act, seeking permission to defend case on all the grounds available to the respondent No.1/insured/owner of the car.
When the respondent No.2/insurance company sought permission to defend the case on all the grounds available to respondent No.1/owner and insured of the car, it is also responsible to satisfy all the responsibilities of respondent No.1/owner/insured of the car.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insured and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 are liable to pay compensation and awards are to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, I answer Issue No.4 in both the cases accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The Petitions filed under Section 166 of IMV Act, by the petitioners are hereby partly allowed in the following terms:
In MVC No.1035/2022, the respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.75,99,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Lakhs Ninety Nine Thousand only) with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
In MVC No.1036/2022, the respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.36,95,500/- (Rupees Thirty Six Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Five Hundred only) SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w 1036/2022 with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending car bearing No.KA-05-MU-9129 shall deposit the compensation amount within three month from today.
In both the cases, compensation and interest are distributed among the petitioners equally.
In MVC No.1035/2022, after deposit of compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allocated in favour of petitioner No.1/wife and Petitioners No.5 & 6/parents of deceased Kheta Ram may be released by crediting the same to their bank account directly.
Entire compensation amount and interest allocation in favour of petitioners No.2 to 4 (minors Kum.Varsha, Master Prathvi raj and Master Bhavesh)/children of deceased Kheta Ram, shall be deposited in any nationalised/scheduled bank in their names till they attain the age of 19 years,
without permitting to create any encumbrance, reserving liberty to their mother to withdraw periodical interest once in three months as per law.
SCCH-1 MVC No.1035/2022 c/w  1036/2022 In MVC No.1036/2022, after deposit of compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allocated in favour of petitioner No.1/wife and Petitioner No.5/father of the deceased Kheema Ram, may be released by crediting the same to their bank account directly.
Entire compensation amount and interest allocation in favour of petitioners No.2 to 4 (minors Kum.Jasavanthika, Kum.Megha and Kum.Motu)/children of deceased Kheema Ram shall be deposited in any nationalised/scheduled bank in their names till they attain the age of 19 years,
without permitting to create any encumbrance, reserving liberty to their mother to withdraw periodical interest once in three months as per law.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- in each case .
